records.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension: build options and unicode61 tokenizer
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream FTS5 documentation read 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. FTS5 inclusion since SQLite 3.9.0; current observed SQLite release recorded in S06.
records.locator: Sections 2.1 (build configuration) and 4.3.1 (unicode61 tokenization/diacritics), especially lines 226-229 and 454-466.
records.observed_operation: FTS5 module build/activation; tokenization of indexed and queried text with the unicode61 tokenizer.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 is included in the SQLite amalgamation since 3.9.0. Source-tree configure currently needs --enable-fts5; amalgamation defaults differ and may change. unicode61 is default, based on Unicode 6.1; spaces/punctuation are separators, letter/number/private-use categories are tokens, matching is Unicode 6.1 case-insensitive, Latin diacritics are removed by default. remove_diacritics=2 handles the documented multi-diacritic exception for Latin; normalization is not language-universal.
records.applicability: Supports a runtime/build probe and a deliberate tokenizer policy only. The application SQLite binding, bundled/system library, target build flags, and actual component version are unknown; verify on Linux and Windows before claiming capability.

records.title: SQLite FTS5 query syntax and string quoting
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream FTS5 documentation read 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. Validate against the SQLite version actually shipped.
records.locator: Sections 3 and 3.1, especially lines 253-279; query-language summary includes phrase, NEAR, column qualifier, grouping, AND/OR/NOT. Embedded double quotes inside an FTS5 quoted string are doubled.
records.observed_operation: Parsing the string supplied to MATCH as an FTS5 expression, including phrase quoting and Boolean/column syntax.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The right-hand MATCH value is itself a query language, not plain literal text. Unquoted syntax characters and operators have engine semantics. Quoted strings use double quotes; an embedded double quote is escaped by doubling it.
records.applicability: Justifies parsing a small product grammar and generating/binding only serialized AST terms or phrases; binding a MATCH string does not restrict FTS5 operators. Do not expose full FTS5 grammar unless explicitly designed.

records.title: SQLite FTS5 external-content tables, triggers, consistency, repair
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream FTS5 documentation read 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. Revalidate against the shipped SQLite release.
records.observed_operation: Read contentless and contentless-delete update/delete behavior; external-content value retrieval; trigger maintenance; rank=1 integrity-check; rebuild from content table.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: A standard contentless table does not support UPDATE/DELETE and its delete command needs original text. Since SQLite 3.43.0, contentless_delete=1 supports DELETE and INSERT OR REPLACE and UPDATE only when all user-defined columns are supplied; it does not support the FTS5 delete command. External content stores index entries but fetches column values from its same-database content table; consistency is the application responsibility. Triggers do not backfill old rows. integrity-check compares an external table only with rank=1. rebuild discards and regenerates from a content table but is not available for contentless tables.
records.applicability: Supports the correction that standard contentless is not update/delete-capable while contentless-delete is version-gated. External content avoids a second body copy and can supply snippets from canonical SQLite content; it is the better first fit when simple rebuild and trigger consistency matter. The app version and content-table write operations are unknown; validate both targets.

records.title: SQLite FTS5 BM25 and snippet functions
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream FTS5 documentation read 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. Revalidate on the selected SQLite release.
records.locator: Sections 5.1.1 and 5.1.3, especially lines 801-810 and 863-870.
records.observed_operation: BM25 result scoring/order and extraction of a selected snippet fragment with match and truncation markers.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 BM25 returns lower numeric values for better matches. snippet() accepts a column choice, match markers, omission marker, and a positive token limit up to 64. Match markers are inserted into the text fragment and are not an HTML safety mechanism.
records.applicability: Supports a lexical ranking and bounded excerpt option. Add a canonical note-ID tie-break and render excerpts as text or escaped markup; do not imply semantic rank or safe HTML.

records.title: SQLite is Transactional
records.released_version_or_commit: Live SQLite documentation read 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. Detailed behavior is configuration/VFS/filesystem dependent; see S16 and S17.
records.locator: Overview lines 20-28, including single-transaction atomicity claims and crash-test harness description.
records.observed_operation: Atomic application of changes within one SQLite transaction during program/OS crash or power loss.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to changes in one SQLite transaction, with the storage/VFS and journal conditions described by SQLite. It is not an atomic transaction spanning SQLite plus a separate Tantivy directory.
records.applicability: Supports co-transactional source-row and FTS trigger work when they are in the same SQLite database/transaction; does not provide dual-write atomicity for a sidecar index.

records.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexWriter and IndexReader APIs
records.released_version_or_commit: Tantivy 0.26.2, released 2026-09-08; tag commit in S07.

records.observed_operation: IndexWriter commit/rollback/add/delete publication and persistence; IndexReader searcher reload after commit.

Delete affects prior-committed and earlier-same-commit documents and is visible only after commit. OnCommitWithDelay reader reload policy is the default and may take tens of milliseconds.

records.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 tokenizer module
records.released_version_or_commit: Tantivy 0.26.2, released 2026-09-08; tag commit in S07.
records.locator: Default/en_stem tokenizer descriptions around lines 59-69; custom TextAnalyzer example around 74-121; AsciiFoldingFilter and SimpleTokenizer descriptions around 122-148.
records.observed_operation: Token stream construction for indexed and query text, including whitespace/punctuation splitting, lowercasing, long-token filtering, stemming and ASCII folding.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Default tokenizer splits at punctuation/whitespace, lowercases, and removes over-limit tokens; docs describe the default limit as 40 characters. RemoveLongFilter's API describes its limit in UTF-8 bytes. ASCII folding is an explicit filter and only maps characters with an ASCII equivalent. English stemming is optional and English-oriented.
records.applicability: Select a named explicit analyzer and test its behavior against FTS5 and representative languages. Do not rely on the default silently dropping long terms or claim accent equivalence.

records.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream WAL documentation read 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. Current observed SQLite release in S06; revalidate selected runtime configuration.
records.locator: Sections 1-4, especially lines 63-85, 91-114, 117-139.
records.observed_operation: Commit a transaction by appending a commit record to the WAL; checkpoint to the database; open and recover a WAL-mode database.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Connection default journal_mode is DELETE; WAL is opt-in and persistent. WAL uses a default 1000-page checkpoint threshold, needs same-host shared memory and does not work over network filesystems, permits one writer, and requires keeping `-wal` with the database. `synchronous=FULL` syncs each commit; NORMAL omits that sync and can lose recent commits after power failure/hard reset.
records.applicability: If WAL is used, keep local files together and record journal/synchronous mode. This task's local SQLite DB fits same-host usage; power-loss durability still depends on selected setting and filesystem.

records.title: SQLite Atomic Commit in rollback-journal mode
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite documentation read 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. The page explicitly applies to rollback mode, not WAL.
records.locator: Introduction and sections 3-4 and 8-9, including VFS/fsync assumptions, hot-journal recovery, crash tests, and failure cases.
records.observed_operation: Commit/rollback a single database-file transaction and recover an incomplete transaction after OS crash or power failure.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The article applies only in rollback mode. It assumes filesystem/file-delete and VFS flush behavior; broken fsync, locking, renamed hot journals, or damaged hardware/filesystems can defeat assumptions. Do not use it as a blanket durability guarantee for every device.
records.applicability: Provides the rollback-mode caveat for crash-recovery design. Test the actual journal mode, VFS and target OS; WAL conditions are in S16.

records.title: SQLite FTS5 documentation: build, tokenizers, content modes, triggers, repair, snippets
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite documentation inspected 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. Investigator's S06 records the 3.53.4 upstream source snapshot, not the app deployment.
records.locator: Sections 2.1, 3 and 3.1, 4.3.1, 4.4.1-4.4.4, 5.1.3, 6.7, 6.12; especially FTS5 build options, unicode61, contentless-delete, external-content trigger examples, REPLACE limitation on the FTS virtual table, rank=1 integrity-check, and rebuild.
records.observed_operation: Opened and inspected current page sections on build activation, query strings, tokenization, contentless/contentless-delete/external-content table semantics, trigger-based consistency, backfill gaps, integrity-check, rebuild, and snippet limits.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 source-tree configure currently requires --enable-fts5 while amalgamation defaults differ and may change. Ordinary contentless tables reject SQL UPDATE/DELETE and return NULL for columns other than rowid; contentless-delete is documented as available since 3.43.0 and permits DELETE, INSERT OR REPLACE, and UPDATE only when all user-defined columns receive values, but not the FTS delete command. External-content tables fetch values from a named same-database content table; consistency remains the application’s responsibility, trigger creation does not index old rows, rank=1 is needed for external-content comparison, and rebuild uses the content table. The FTS5 page says new code should prefer contentless-delete over ordinary contentless; this is not a universal preference over external-content.
records.applicability: Supports conditional FTS5 design claims and correct distinctions among three table modes only. Actual app library, configuration, table schema, and writes are unverified; the current live page is not a deployment-version pin.

records.title: SQLite ON CONFLICT REPLACE semantics
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite documentation; page reports last updated 2025-11-22 13:15:11Z; no versioned release URL.
records.locator: REPLACE subsection, especially lines 42-48.
records.observed_operation: Checked behavior of INSERT OR REPLACE when a unique or primary-key conflict deletes a pre-existing row before inserting the replacement.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite documents that delete triggers caused by REPLACE fire if and only if recursive triggers are enabled. This is specific to rows deleted by the REPLACE conflict strategy; it does not describe ordinary UPDATE or DELETE statements.
records.applicability: Applies to the proposed canonical-note trigger design only if the actual note write path uses REPLACE. No such app operation was observed.

records.title: SQLite recursive_triggers pragma
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite pragma documentation inspected 2026-10-10; the page says recursive-trigger support arrived in 3.6.18 and was initially OFF for compatibility, and says the default may change.
records.locator: PRAGMA recursive_triggers section, lines 723-734.
records.observed_operation: Checked the connection-scoped setting that governs whether REPLACE-induced deletes fire delete triggers.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The pragma can be queried or set on a database connection. Historical default was OFF; SQLite permits a future default change, so a design must inspect/configure the exact runtime instead of relying on an assumed default.
records.applicability: Makes the REPLACE trigger caveat testable on each shipped connection; does not establish the application setting.

records.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexWriter API

source_conflicts.topic: SQLite recursive-trigger default and REPLACE delete triggers
source_conflicts.observation: The 3.6.18 release record says REPLACE delete triggers require recursive triggers. Historical oldnews forecast a recursive-by-default change in 3.7.0; the 3.7.0 release summary does not list such a change. Current pragma documentation says recursive triggers were initially OFF and may be turned on in future releases. Build configuration can also change initial behavior. An upstream Fossil source artifact shows the guarded macro default is 0 when undefined, but its exact release association is not exposed and compile flags can override it.
source_conflicts.resolution: The consequence is conditional and supported; the deployment default is not asserted. Query/configure the actual connection before prepared statements or rule out REPLACE on indexed note rows, then test the chosen operation. The macro artifact is corroborating source evidence only, not a deployed-version pin.

source_conflicts.observation: Current FTS5 docs say new code should prefer contentless-delete over ordinary contentless, while external-content tables have separate same-database value lookup, trigger, integrity-check, and content rebuild semantics.
source_conflicts.resolution: These are not conflicting recommendations: the wording compares contentless-delete to ordinary contentless, not external content. External content remains the conditional preference for this adapter's excerpt/rebuild needs; exact app release/build is unknown.

source_conflicts.topic: Tantivy malformed query and mutable latest docs

source_conflicts.observation: The writer API applies explicit document operations and makes them visible on commit; it has no link to external SQLite relation changes.
source_conflicts.resolution: Inference: if collection values are indexed in a sidecar document and membership changes separately in SQLite, a durable event must refresh that document or results can be stale while the watermark appears complete. The app tag schema is unknown.
